rows.name: Drawing vs Spec Checker
rows.summary: Automate drawing-versus-spec comparison with deterministic extraction and AI-assisted discrepancy review.
rows.impact: Design, project management, installation, and operations teams.
rows.needs: Catch discrepancies early and make the output easy to trust and act on.
rows.friction: If the AI hides evidence or over-infers, users lose confidence in the audit.
rows.helpfulAction: Package the stable workflow and test the remaining edge cases.

rows.name: Local AI Infrastructure
rows.summary: Maintain the local Ollama, LibreChat, models, and evaluation environment used for internal experimentation.
rows.needs: A local stack that is easy to reproduce, update, and understand.
rows.friction: One-off model and configuration changes can make the environment difficult to reproduce.
rows.helpfulAction: Document the stable baseline and archive experiments that are no longer needed.

rows.name: Recruiting Agent
rows.summary: Automate candidate discovery, verification, enrichment, and controlled outreach preparation.
rows.impact: Hiring managers, recruiting stakeholders, and candidates.
rows.needs: Reduce repetitive sourcing work while keeping sensitive decisions under human review.
rows.friction: Automating too far can turn a quality recruiting workflow into noisy outreach.
rows.helpfulAction: Finish the candidate review queue and define the approval boundary before outreach.

rows.name: AI Requests / Random Problems
rows.summary: Hold small AI requests and experiments until they become real projects or are closed.
rows.needs: Clarify the business need before investing engineering time.
rows.friction: Starting implementation before understanding the desired outcome creates unnecessary work.
rows.helpfulAction: Triage the newest requests and close or promote each one.

rows.name: IT Workforce Agent
rows.summary: Turn IT conversations and support activity into a living project and ticket system with minimal manual maintenance.
rows.impact: IT operations and employees who need support.
rows.needs: Capture context automatically without creating another system that has to be babysat.
rows.friction: A tracker that requires duplicate data entry will stop being useful quickly.
rows.helpfulAction: Finish the Cloudflare-backed tracker and connect the first automated update source.

rows.name: Azure & Cloud Migration
rows.summary: Move shared infrastructure toward Azure while reducing dependency on DC1 and preserving reliable file access.
rows.impact: Staff using shared drives, project files, VPN, and legacy server resources.
rows.needs: A migration that feels boring to users: reliable access, clear rollback paths, and minimal downtime.
rows.friction: Running cloud and on-prem processes in parallel longer than necessary can create confusion.
rows.helpfulAction: Finish the dependency inventory and pick the next workload that can safely leave DC1.

rows.name: CMMC Level 2
rows.summary: Close control gaps, gather evidence, and make security requirements repeatable across the company.
rows.impact: Leadership, employees, customers, and compliance partners.
rows.needs: Security controls that are understandable, auditable, and do not create unnecessary user friction.
rows.friction: Policies that exist only on paper or controls that are difficult for employees to follow.
rows.helpfulAction: Turn the next highest-risk gap into a documented, testable control.

rows.name: Identity & Endpoint Management
rows.summary: Standardize Entra-joined devices, onboarding, account lifecycle, and access to company resources.
rows.impact: Every employee receiving, replacing, or signing into a company device.
rows.needs: New users can sign in and work with minimal manual intervention.
rows.friction: Legacy profiles and mixed identity methods make troubleshooting harder than it should be.
rows.helpfulAction: Finish the standard onboarding checklist and test it on the next new hire.

rows.name: Network & Infrastructure
rows.summary: Keep office networking, VPN, switching, Wi-Fi, servers, and monitoring predictable and supportable.
rows.needs: Reliable connectivity with enough visibility to diagnose problems quickly.
rows.friction: Troubleshooting from memory instead of a current network map wastes time.
rows.helpfulAction: Finish the live network map and attach recovery notes for critical services.

rows.name: Phoenix Office
rows.summary: Finish the remaining network, ISP, vendor, and infrastructure items for the Phoenix office.
rows.impact: Phoenix office employees and visiting staff.
rows.needs: Stable wired and wireless access without temporary workarounds.
rows.friction: Open vendor dependencies can leave users unsure which issues are temporary versus permanent.
rows.helpfulAction: Close the remaining provider item and publish the final office network state.

rows.name: IT Support / Random Problems
rows.summary: Catch day-to-day issues that are real work but do not yet justify their own project.
rows.needs: Resolve the user’s actual blocker quickly and promote recurring patterns into projects.
rows.friction: Treating recurring incidents as isolated tickets hides systemic problems.
rows.helpfulAction: Clear the highest-impact open ticket and identify any pattern worth promoting.
